subtasks.description: Declare FIFO_RX_MEM_DEPTH and FIFO_RX_MEM_ADR_SIZE parameters; define RAM storage as an explicitly unrolled set of 32-bit scalar registers (ram_0, ram_1, …); declare write pointer adr_i and read pointer adr_o with extra high‑bit for wrap‑around detection; declare 32‑bit nibble accumulator tmp, 8‑bit byte‑write‑enable we, and 1‑bit data‑written flag ft. All register widths must match spec S005.
constraints: RAM must be flattened into scalar 32‑bit registers explicitly named ram_0, ram_1, …, ram_<DEPTH‑1>; do not use Verilog unpacked arrays, multidimensional references, generate, or genvar.
Pointer registers adr_i and adr_o must include one additional high‑bit beyond FIFO_RX_MEM_ADR_SIZE for full/empty wrap‑around detection.

subtasks.description: On wclk rising edge, when wr is high, accumulate 4‑bit d into tmp according to we’s current bit position; shift we left by one bit to track nibble accumulation; when we overflows (all 8 nibbles written), write tmp into RAM at adr_i, set ft, and increment adr_i with wrap‑around and high‑bit toggle. On reset, clear tmp to 0, we to 8’h1, ft to 0, and adr_i to 0.
constraints: Use explicit scalar RAM signals (ram_0, ram_1, …) with conditional write logic; no unpacked arrays or generates.
Nibble packing order must be consistent with we’s initial value 8’h1 and left‑shift behavior; start from the rightmost nibble of tmp.
Wrap‑around must toggle the extended high‑bit of adr_i when adr_i increments from (DEPTH‑1) back to 0.

subtasks.description: On rclk rising edge, if rd is high and empty is deasserted, increment adr_o with wrap‑around and high‑bit toggle; present q as the 32‑bit data from the RAM location indexed by adr_o (either combinational or registered). When empty, hold the last valid read data; ensure adr_o does not change during empty reads.
constraints: Access RAM using scalar signals (ram_0, ram_1, …) with multiplexer logic; no unpacked arrays or generates.
If q is registered, ensure the register updates only on valid reads and the Q output remains stable when empty.
Wrap‑around must toggle the extended high‑bit of adr_o when adr_o increments from (DEPTH‑1) back to 0.

subtasks.description: Generate full, empty, and mem_empt flags. Synchronize write pointer adr_i into rclk domain and read pointer adr_o into wclk domain using at least 2‑stage flip‑flop chains. Derive full (wclk domain) by comparing synchronized read pointer with write pointer; derive empty (rclk domain) by comparing synchronized write pointer with read pointer; compute mem_empt as available word count from pointer difference. All comparisons must use extended high‑bit to correctly handle wrap‑around.
constraints: Synchronize each pointer bit using dedicated 2‑stage flip‑flops; do not use continuous assignments or bypass paths; split multi‑bit pointers into scalar stages to avoid unpacked arrays.
Pointer comparisons must explicitly compare both the address portion and the extended high‑bit to distinguish full vs. empty when base addresses are equal.
mem_empt must be a combinational function of the synchronized pointers (provided as 2‑bit output) and should be glitch‑free after synchronizer settling.

subtasks.description: If q and mem_empt are not already driven in B3 or B4, provide purely combinational assignments: q from the RAM location selected by adr_o (or its registered equivalent), and mem_empt from the synchronized pointer difference. Ensure the outputs align with the interface contract in S004.
constraints: Use only continuous assignments; no sequential logic.
If RAM is already flattened into scalars (ram_0, …), use a multiplexer expression for q; avoid unpacked arrays.
Omit generation of any signal already assigned in a prior block.
